Repair and extend the eMicro CPU control-plane project in `/workspace/project`.
The supplied multi-file system uses a real FAdo compiler, state exporter and map loader.
Make the pipeline compile policies into canonical live-state images and replay causal events.
Implement atomic image publication, pinned versions and exact resource accounting.
Support multiplexed requests, cloned process identities, transport and file-mediated handoffs.
The complete schema, language, boundaries and output semantics are in `/workspace/PROTOCOL.md`.
This is an offline userspace abstraction; kernel attachment and service deployment are excluded.
The whole `/workspace/project` directory is the deliverable; additional ordinary files are allowed.
Keep `driver.py` as the JSON entry point; internal implementation choices are yours.
`python3 /workspace/launch.py` reads one request from stdin and writes one response to stdout.
Use only the supplied Python 3.11 runtime, standard library and pinned offline dependencies.
Do not install packages or require network access, threads, subprocesses or external services.
Verification executes the collected project read-only as a nonroot user with fresh state.
Only `/workspace/tmp` is writable; 2 GiB memory and 256 MiB stdout limits are public.
The two-minute CPU budget applies to the entire maximum batch, including compilation and replay.
Run `python3 /workspace/public_check.py` as the image's nonroot user for a small CLI sanity check.
The starter is incomplete; passing the public sanity check does not cover the full contract.


Work in /workspace. When finished run exactly: echo COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT

All verification passes. Here's a summary of the completed work:

## Deliverable: `/workspace/project` (8 files, 58 KB)

**`driver.py`** — JSON entry point
- Strict envelope: 24 MiB cap, UTF-8/BOM, duplicate keys, nonfinite & overflowing float tokens, 4300-digit integer tokens (pinned interpreter limit), container nesting ≤ 64 measured on string-stripped text, exact top-level schema, ≤4 jobs.
- Static per-job validation (services/limits/events schema & types) → job-scoped `{"error":"invalid"}`; whole-request budgets (200 000 events, 16 stages, 8 MiB policies, 32 768 atoms, 65 536 path services) summed over *structurally valid* jobs only.
- Streams compact ASCII JSON in 1 MiB chunks (peak RSS ≈ 250 MB for a 102 MiB response), flushes, `os._exit(0)`.

**`syntax.py`** — byte-filtered tokenizer (rejects vertical tab / all non-listed whitespace) + context-sensitive recursive-descent parser, so services legitimately named `match`, `and`, `allow`… work in paths. Enforces depth ≤16, path ≤16, ≤8 complex rules × ≤32 atoms, ≤4 distinct non-`match` atoms (path ≤4), 32 768 atoms / 65 536 path services, plus derived token/length envelopes so hostile strings fail fast.

**`compiler/compiler.py`** — serial reduction: per-atom complete DFAs (KMP for `endswith`/`contains`), hash-consed negation-normal-form residual expressions, memoised Brzozowski derivatives explored breadth-first, dead-residual contraction, partition-refinement minimisation with a *sound* early oversize abort, then canonical BFS renumbering in increasing label order with `DENY=4294967295`; empty language → one false flag/all-DENY row, all-allow → one true flag/zero row, >8192 rows rejected.

**`ebpf/helper.py`** — `MemoryMap` CPU backend + `Agent` with all 16 ops: atomic stage/commit/retire, spawn/clone/exit with per-pair generation high-water marks, begin/finish with monotone request marks, open/send/recv/close with stream marks, retained packets, receipts, exact 24-byte wire tags, store/load/unlink inode generations, and exact reference/cell/capacity accounting; every rejection is a provable no-op.

**Validation performed:** public check, exact sanity fixture, 8 hand-written suites (lifecycle, transport, files, validation, bounds, policy syntax, u32 exhaustion, atomicity), plus differential fuzzing against two independent references — a naive recomputing runtime model (~500 rounds) and a brute-force Myhill-Nerode oracle / FAdo-based canonicaliser (~2000 policies, 0 mismatches). Max-envelope batch (200 000 events, 16 images, 102 MiB stdout) runs in ~3.8 s wall under the real seccomp/rlimit child guard.
